Debunking Power Supply Myths

A properly sized power supply will be more efficient when the system is operating at peak load. They're all pretty inefficient at idle.

Why do you say an oversized PSU will last longer? If you've got a source for that info, please share it. I usually shoot for a rating of 10% more than the system's peak load, and that has served me well. If lifetime is your concern, look for build quality versus just getting a bigger one.

Actually, both are important for long life. Running a system nearing the peak load of the PSU will result in shorter life. Most people target about 30% higher for good reason. First, capacitors degrade over time. It doesn't matter who made it, or what the quality is, they degrade. Simple fact of life. So do the supporting electronic components. Resistors, transistors, etc all degrade over time. Usually, the end result is lower total available power output. Also, by buying a bit larger than necessary, you avoid more waste in the future if you need more power. Then there is overclocking, which takes even more power.

And in the end, an 850W Platinum rated PSU will still use the same amount of power as that 450W unit both at load and idle.
